messages.subject: cleaning up a plot
parts:
I am trying to clean up a set of forest plots.  

Thus far, thanks to suggestions on this list serve, I have 3 to 4 parameters that I am plotting (pharmacokinetic parameters) for 4 different drugs using a coord_flip + geom_errorbar to display the fold-change in each parameter in different conditions.  

iv.mdz2<-ggplot(ivmdz2, aes(x=Parameter, y=Mean, ymin=Lo, ymax=Hi))
iv.mdz2<-iv.mdz2+geom_errorbar()+coord_flip()+geom_hline(aes(yintercept=0), lty=2)+xlab('Parameter') +ylab("Fold Change with 90% CI") + geom_point(aes(x=Parameter, y=Mean), size=8, shape=5)+theme_bw()
iv.mdz2<-iv.mdz2+scale_y_continuous(limits=c(-1,3))+ opts(title="xxx")
iv.mdz2

For publication, I would like to both plot 4 of these plots in a grid, with the parameter name on the x, and the fold change on the y (mock-up below).   To do this, I need to be able to re-order the parameters, and fit this to a facet_grid.   Any help in this would be appreciated.  

Thanks

--
R. Matthew Strother, MD
Clinical Pharmacology
Medical Oncology

On Tue, Apr 24, 2012 at 1:58 PM, Robert Strother <rstr...@gmail.com> wrote:
I am trying to clean up a set of forest plots.  

Thus far, thanks to suggestions on this list serve, I have 3 to 4 parameters that I am plotting (pharmacokinetic parameters) for 4 different drugs using a coord_flip + geom_errorbar to display the fold-change in each parameter in different conditions.  

iv.mdz2<-ggplot(ivmdz2, aes(x=Parameter, y=Mean, ymin=Lo, ymax=Hi))
iv.mdz2<-iv.mdz2+geom_errorbar()+coord_flip()+geom_hline(aes(yintercept=0), lty=2)+xlab('Parameter') +ylab("Fold Change with 90% CI") + geom_point(aes(x=Parameter, y=Mean), size=8, shape=5)+theme_bw()
iv.mdz2<-iv.mdz2+scale_y_continuous(limits=c(-1,3))+ opts(title="xxx")
iv.mdz2

For publication, I would like to both plot 4 of these plots in a grid, with the parameter name on the x, and the fold change on the y (mock-up below).   To do this, I need to be able to re-order the parameters, and fit this to a facet_grid.   Any help in this would be appreciated.

(a) If you want the factor as the x and the fold change as the y, then don't use coord_flip().
(b) To reorder the factor levels, redefine Parameter as an ordered factor in ivmdz2, e.g.,
       ivmdz2$Parameter <- factor(ivmdz2$Parameter, levels = c('AUC', 'CL', 'T1/2', 'V'))
(c) You don't have two grouping variables AFAICS, so to get a 2 x 2 arrangement of plots per below, you'd want to use facet_wrap() instead, where the grouping variable needs to be defined in ivmdz2 beforehand (say gp). Assuming this is the case, the code snippet would be something like
   ... + facet_wrap(~ gp, ncol = 2)

HTH,
Dennis
Thanks

--
R. Matthew Strother, MD

messages.author: f4249b01b99d0091
messages.subject: Re: cleaning up a plot
parts: >For publication, I would like to both plot 4 of these plots in a grid, with the parameter name on the x, and the fold change on the y (mock-up below).   To do this, I need to be able to re-order the parameters, and fit this to a facet_grid.   Any help in this would be appreciated.

Robert, here's my first crack at it. See code below.
Regards,
Ben


d <- read.csv("ivmdz2.csv")

library( ggplot2 )
library( grid )

p <- ggplot( d, aes( x=Parameter, y=Mean, ymin=Lo, ymax=Hi ) )

p <- p + geom_errorbar() + coord_flip() + geom_hline( aes( yintercept=0 ), lty=2 ) 
p <- p + xlab( 'Parameter' ) +ylab( "Fold Change with 90% CI" ) + geom_point( size=3, shape=5 )
p <- p + scale_y_continuous( limits=c( -1, 3 ) ) + opts( title="xxx" )
p <- p + facet_wrap( ~Drug, nrow=2, ncol=2 )
p <- p + theme_bw() + opts( strip.text.x=theme_blank(), strip.background=theme_blank() )

print( p )

grid.text( "A", 0.16, 0.9, gp=gpar( fontface="bold" ) )      # A-D annotations
grid.text( "B", 0.58, 0.9, gp=gpar( fontface="bold" ) )
grid.text( "C", 0.16, 0.47, gp=gpar( fontface="bold" ) )
grid.text( "D", 0.58, 0.47, gp=gpar( fontface="bold" ) )

messages.author: f4249b01b99d0091
messages.subject: Re: cleaning up a plot
parts:
> This works well.  Is there a way to remove the unused parameter labels by row in the grid?

Ugh, this starts to get ugly; pretty sure you need to use multiple
viewports for this kind of thing. I guess I'd do it something like
below, which should get you started, but you'll want to adjust the
grid.layout values and plot margins so things line up and look nice.
As far as I know, trial and error is the only way here.

Good luck-

Ben


d <- read.csv("ivmdz2.csv")

library(ggplot2)
library(grid)

# First, build the four panels
plots <- list(NULL)
theme_set(theme_bw())
for(i in unique(d$Drug)) {
d1 <- droplevels(subset(d, Drug==i, drop=T))
p <- ggplot(d1, aes(x=Parameter, y=Mean, ymin=Lo, ymax=Hi))
p <- p + geom_point(size=3, shape=5) + geom_errorbar() +
coord_flip() + geom_hline(aes(yintercept=0), lty=2) +
scale_y_continuous(limits=c(-1, 3))
plots[[i]] <- p
}

#pdf("ivmdz2.pdf", width=4, height=6)
grid.newpage()
pushViewport(viewport(layout=grid.layout(2, 2)))
vplayout<-function(x, y) viewport(layout.pos.row=x, layout.pos.col=y)

# Now plot them in the four regions, adjusting margins and axis text
as necessary
print(plots[["DRUG 1"]] + opts(plot.margin=unit(c(1,0,0,0), "lines"),
axis.text.x=theme_blank(), axis.title.x=theme_blank()),
vp=vplayout(1,1))
print(plots[["DRUG 2"]] + opts(plot.margin=unit(c(1,1,0,0), "lines"),
axis.text.x=theme_blank(), axis.title.x=theme_blank(),
axis.title.y=theme_blank()), vp=vplayout(1,2))
print(plots[["DRUG 3"]] + opts(plot.margin=unit(c(0,0,0,0), "lines")),
vp=vplayout(2,1))
print(plots[["DRUG 4"]] + opts(plot.margin=unit(c(0,1,0,0), "lines"),
axis.title.y=theme_blank()), vp=vplayout(2,2))

#dev.off()
